cohort: 19,842 women who gave birth over a 10-year period
finding: Labours that started at night were associated with a higher rate of normal deliveries, lower rates of caesarean sections and labour augmentation, and shorter first stage duration compared to labours starting during the day.
mod_finding: Night-onset labours had fewer caesarean sections (8.7% vs. 10.1%) compared to day-onset labours.
